title: Right Triangle Similarity and the Geometric Mean
seo_title: Geometry Right Triangle Similarity and Geometric Mean Worksheets (TEKS G.8B)
standard_text: G.8B identify and apply the relationships that exist when an altitude is drawn to the hypotenuse of a right triangle, including the geometric mean, to solve problems
meta_desc: Free Geometry worksheets for Texas TEKS G.8B: the geometric mean, the altitude to the hypotenuse, the leg rule and similar right triangles. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • The geometric mean of a and b is √(ab).
  • The altitude to the hypotenuse makes three similar right triangles.
  • Altitude rule: the altitude is the geometric mean of the two hypotenuse segments.
  • Leg rule: each leg is the geometric mean of the whole hypotenuse and the segment next to that leg.

Examples

Example

Segments 4 and 9

√(4 × 9) = √36

Answer: altitude 6

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Averaging insteadMultiply, then take the square root.
Using the wrong segment for a legUse the segment next to the leg.
Forgetting the square root√36 = 6, not 36.

faq.a: Each shares an angle with the big triangle and has a right angle (AA).

CD is the altitude to the hypotenuse. CD = 6 and AD = 18. Find DB.
items.e: CD² = AD × DB, so 36 = 18 × DB and DB = 36 ÷ 18 = 2.
